clue.text: Modest female featured in Reeve's Tale

indicators.note: a thing featured in a story appears within it, so the letters sit inside the words Reeve's Tale

explanation.surface: A demure woman appears as a character in one of Chaucer's Canterbury Tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featured in' tells you the letters run across the end of Reeve's and the start of Tale. The Reeve's Tale is one of Chaucer's Canterbury Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A Vestal virgin was a chaste priestess of Rome, so the word came to mean a pure, chaste woman.

clue.text: Did nag run in steeplechase, finally out of countenance?

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word steeplechase
the word in tells us the letter for run is placed inside the rest

parts.note: to be out of countenance is to be disconcerted or embarrassed, abashed
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A horse in a steeplechase stumbles at the end, looking embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: Nag looks like a horse in a racing scene, but it is a verb, to scold persistently.
explanation.definitionFit: To earbash is to talk at someone relentlessly, to harangue or pester them.

clue.text: Up to limiting male power, what helped women's lib?

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing within bounds, so the till word surrounds the others

parts.note: till means up to, as in 'till midnight'
he is the male pronoun
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A question about what aided feminism, keeping men's power in check.
explanation.definitionFit: The oral contraceptive gave women control over their fertility, a landmark of 1960s feminism.

clue.text: Eating veal or cat is preposterous for me!

definitions.text: Eating veal or cat is preposterous for me!

indicators.note: preposterous means absurd or topsy-turvy, signalling the fodder's letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A diner refuses meat, declaring that veal or cat is out of the question.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is all fifteen letters of EATING VEAL OR CAT; the whole clue is what such a diner would say.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose diet takes in milk and dairy but excludes meat would find eating any animal unacceptable.

clue.text: Winds up in Maine city

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated somewhere in the northeastern United States.
explanation.walkthrough: Maine looks like the US state, but here it is Maine-et-Loire, the French department whose chief city carries this name.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind someone up is to irritate or enrage them; separately, the city is the capital of the French department Maine-et-Loire.

clue.text: Letterhead etc shows name for street holding quite lavish fundraiser

indicators.note: holding means the altered word contains the other pieces inside it
shows N for ST means the name letter replaces the street letters in the stationery word
shows N for ST means the name letter replaces the street letters in the stationery word

parts.note: letterhead, envelopes and the like are stationery
all can mean quite, as in 'all alone'
OTT, over the top, means extravagant or lavish

explanation.surface: Headed notepaper shows a name in place of a street, holding a rather extravagant charity event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows name for street' is an instruction: N replaces ST, giving NATIONERY, and 'holding' then puts ALL and OTT inside it. OTT (over the top) is British slang for excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK's state lottery raises money for good causes from ticket sales.

clue.text: Those within search party leaving edges of Pacific — they failed to find her

indicators.note: leaving means the letters for the edges of Pacific go away
those within the phrase search party are the letters inside it, dropping the outer S and Y

parts.note: the edges of the word Pacific are its first and last letters, P and C, both taken out

explanation.surface: Searchers give up on the Pacific's fringes, having failed to locate a missing woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C and P (the first and last letters of Pacific) from EARCHPART, the inside of search party.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelia Earhart, the pioneering aviator, vanished over the Pacific in 1937 and was never found by searchers.

clue.text: Large group also distressed about hospital

indicators.note: about means going around, so the scrambled word surrounds the hospital letter
distressed means battered or roughed up, signalling the letters of also are rearranged

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Many people, also upset, gather near a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoal is a large group of fish, and by extension any big crowd.

clue.text: Democrat ousted by American tough guy's press

indicators.note: ousted means thrown out, so the Democrat letter is removed

parts.note: hardass is American slang for a tough, uncompromising person
D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A Democrat is thrown out of office by a hard-nosed American, as the media reports.
explanation.walkthrough: Press looks like the newspapers, but it is a verb, to urge persistently.
explanation.definitionFit: To harass someone is to keep pressing or pestering them.

clue.text: Live Aid arranger harbours good impulse

indicators.note: something that harbours another keeps it sheltered inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Midge Ure co-organised the 1985 Live Aid concerts with Bob Geldof

explanation.surface: The organiser of a famous charity concert acted on a generous whim.
explanation.walkthrough: Geldof is the name that springs to mind, but it is his co-organiser Midge Ure whose surname is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge is a sudden strong desire, the same as an impulse.

clue.text: I won't hush up conservative Tea Partier before fight

parts.note: the Mad Hatter hosts the tea party in Alice in Wonderland
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A right-wing American activist refuses to stay quiet before a political battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea Partier suggests the American Tea Party movement, but it is the Mad Hatter from Lewis Carroll's tea party.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who talks incessantly would say of themselves that they will never stop speaking.

clue.text: Uncontrolled state borders as far as British Canadian territory

indicators.note: one piece borders another by lying round its edges, so it surrounds the rest

parts.note: mania is a state of wild, uncontrolled excitement
to means as far as, as in 'up to the gate'

explanation.surface: A lawless region's boundaries stretch right up to a British-held part of Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitoba is one of Canada's prairie provinces, a territorial division of that country.

clue.text: Nothing left in contest for adviser

parts.note: O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

indicators.note: the word in places one letter inside the contest word

parts.note: a race is a contest of speed

explanation.surface: With nothing remaining in the competition, someone seeks counsel.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle was a source of divine counsel in the ancient world, and now means any wise guide.

clue.text: Berry, possibly large, with healthy covering

indicators.note: the healthy word acts as a covering, wrapping around the letter for large

parts.note: hale means healthy, as in 'hale and hearty'
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A fruit, perhaps a big one, with a wholesome skin.
explanation.walkthrough: Berry looks like a fruit, but it is the actress Halle Berry; 'possibly' signals a forename defined by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Halle is the first name of the American actress Halle Berry, so it is one forename that goes with Berry.

clue.text: Headliner's first step in serving tea to crowd?

definitions.note: the definition is the headliner plus 's for 'is', telling the solver what the answer is

parts.note: a start is the first step in a process
an urn is the big vessel used to serve tea to many people at once

explanation.surface: The opening stage of a performer's act involves pouring tea for an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A star turn is the main act on a bill, the performer whose name tops the posters.

clue.text: Person making no effort to pen short song?

definitions.text: Person making no effort to pen short song?

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the resting person surrounds the shortened song

parts.note: a rester is someone who rests, making no effort

indicators.note: short means the final letter of the hymn word is cut off

parts.note: a hymn is a religious song

explanation.surface: Someone too lazy to write even a brief tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a dig at a poor versifier who scribbles little effort into a short song.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymester is a writer of trivial verse, a poetaster who puts in little craft.

clue.text: Ancient king, from the east, prosecutes somebody renouncing inside party

indicators.note: in an across answer, coming from the east means reading right to left, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: to sue someone is to prosecute them in court

indicators.note: giving up its inside leaves only the first and last letters of the word somebody

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A ruler from the Orient takes someone to court for abandoning their party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' turns the whole run SUESSYDO around, since an across answer is normally read from the west; 'renouncing inside' keeps only S and Y of somebody.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus was the legendary king of Ithaca, hero of Homer's Odyssey.

clue.text: Is a springer including one now primarily reared?

definitions.text: Is a springer including one now primarily reared?

indicators.note: in a down answer, reared means raised upward, so the letters are read bottom to top
including means the leaping word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: one who is a springer leaps
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the word now

explanation.surface: A question whether a jumping animal now raised includes one more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts I and N inside LEAPS, giving LEINAPS, which 'reared' turns upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The springer is a breed of gundog that flushes game, one of the spaniel family.

clue.text: Set of rules with not a word on song

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means placed above, so the first piece sits atop the song

parts.note: sh is the sound demanding silence, not a word spoken
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A rulebook with nothing to say about singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharia is Islamic law, a code of conduct governing believers.

clue.text: Trot maybe went speedily at the finish

parts.note: left means went away, departed

indicators.note: at the finish means the final letter of the word speedily

explanation.surface: A horse broke into a quick pace at the end of the race.
explanation.walkthrough: Trot looks like a horse's gait, but it is short for Trotskyist, a left-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trotskyist is a follower of Trotsky, an example of a left-winger, colloquially a lefty.

clue.text: Figure involved with start of blaze?

definitions.text: Figure involved with start of blaze?

parts.words: Figure involved with start of blaze?
parts.note: read as a person who sets a fire going, someone who starts blazes deliberately

explanation.definitionFit: An arsonist is colloquially called by this name, a person obsessed with starting fires.

clue.text: Slips in stage across grass

indicators.note: the stage word lies across the grass word, spanning it on both sides

parts.note: an era is a stage or period in history
to grass is British slang for informing on someone, as is to rat

explanation.surface: Someone loses their footing while crossing a lawn on a theatre platform.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass and rat both mean to inform on someone to the police in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are mistakes in printed matter, small slips listed for correction.

clue.text: John Paul I (and another) backed part of papal regalia in word and picture

parts.note: the Fisherman's Ring is part of a pope's regalia
the letter O pictures a ring, so the regalia appears in word and picture

explanation.surface: A pope's ring from his regalia is reversed and pictured.
explanation.walkthrough: John Paul I looks like a pope, but it is John, Paul and I (another Beatle), backed on drums by the fourth member. RING is spelt out in word and O drawn as its picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer, keeping the beat behind John Lennon, Paul McCartney and George Harrison.

clue.text: Try one out on case of assault?

definitions.text: Try one out on case of assault?

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters, here of assault
out signals the letters of try one are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to test a lawyer on a violence charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the anagram of TRY ONE after AT, the first and last letters of assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer is the one who tries out a case of assault in court, so the whole clue describes the profession.

clue.text: Nestor's after limitless (endless) uninflected word

indicators.note: after places the setter's piece behind the trimmed word
endless says the final letter of the word for limitless is dropped

parts.note: infinite means without limits
Nestor is the setter, so Nestor's is 'I've', the setter saying 'I have'

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of following something with no bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves by their pseudonym; here Nestor's becomes I'VE, I have.
explanation.definitionFit: The infinitive is the base form of a verb, not inflected for person, number or tense.

clue.text: Target vessel and ram end

explanation.surface: Something aimed at, a ship and a charging sheep all reaching a conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A butt is a target of jokes, a large cask, to strike with the head, and the stub end of a cigarette.

clue.text: Old online journal introducing new tablet format?

indicators.note: introducing means the online journal word takes in the letter for new

parts.note: a blog is a journal published online

explanation.surface: An old internet diary brings in a fresh layout for a tablet device.
explanation.walkthrough: Tablet suggests a computer, but a stone or pill tablet is often rectangular.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle longer than it is wide is the usual shape of a tablet of stone or a slab.

clue.text: Turned over carpet crusted with trifle and dairy product

indicators.note: turned over means the whole assembled piece is read in reverse
being crusted with something means having it all round the outside, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: a toy is a trifle, a thing of little value
a rug is a small carpet

explanation.surface: A dessert spilled onto the floor covering, along with some cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crusted with' wraps the trifle word round the carpet word, making TRUGOY, and 'Turned over' then reverses it all; 'trifle' is a small thing, not the pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogurt is a fermented milk food, sold among dairy goods.
